source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts - Game of 24
finding: GPT-4 with ToT solves far more Game of 24 than chain of thought, and more than 100 CoT samples.
numbers: 100 test problems. IO 7.3%, CoT 4.0%, CoT-SC k=100 9.0%, ToT b=1 45%, ToT b=5 74%. Best of 100 CoT 49%, best of 100 IO 33%. About 60% of CoT samples already failed at the first step.
limits: One task, GPT-4, 100 problems. Thought steps and the sure/maybe/impossible value prompt are hand tuned. Experiments run May 2023.
agent_relevance: Search with pruning beats blind resampling at equal node count because early wrong steps are cut. Fits S6 only where steps can be checked.

source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts - cost
finding: ToT costs about as many tokens as 100 CoT trials but beats them. On creative writing it costs about 5x tokens.
numbers: Game of 24: ToT 5.5k completion + 1.4k prompt tokens, $0.74 per case, 74%. CoT best of 100: 6.7k + 2.2k tokens, $0.47, 49%. IO best of 100: $0.13, 33%. Creative writing: about 5x tokens and cost.
limits: Prices are May 2023 API rates. The authors expect costs to fall.
agent_relevance: Budget a tree at about 100 plain samples and compare to that, not to one sample.

source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts - Mini Crosswords ablations
finding: Depth-first search with backtracking and pruning lifts 5x5 crosswords from near zero to partial success. Backtracking matters most.
numbers: 20 test games from GooBix. Word success: IO and CoT under 16%, ToT 60%. Letters: CoT 38.7 vs ToT 78. Games solved 4/20. Oracle best state: 7/20 games, 67.5% words. No pruning: 41.5% words. No backtracking: 20% words.
limits: Only 20 games. DFS capped at 100 steps. The rule that picks the output state is weak (the oracle gains a lot).
agent_relevance: Keep both pruning and backtracking in S6.

source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts - Creative Writing and weaker models
finding: On open-ended writing ToT gives a small gain. A weaker GPT-3.5 evaluator keeps most of the Game of 24 gain, a weaker generator does not.
numbers: Coherence score (GPT-4 judge): IO 6.19, ToT 7.56, ToT with refine 7.91. GPT-3.5 ToT on Game of 24: 19%. GPT-4 generate + GPT-3.5 evaluate: 64%.
limits: Judge is GPT-4, same family as the generator.
agent_relevance: Evaluation can be cheap; the generator must be strong. Roles can be split in code.

source: Long (2023) Large Language Model Guided Tree-of-Thought
finding: A controller with a checker and memory module lets an LLM backtrack in Sudoku. Independent concurrent ToT.
numbers: Sudoku: ToT solver success rate 80% higher than one-shot/few-shot on the 4x4 set and 60% higher on 5x5 (as the paper writes it). Failed 1 of 10 puzzles at 4x4 and 2 on 5x5 within the 100-round cap.
limits: Small home-built puzzle set. A rule-based controller cannot tell whether a board can still be completed.
agent_relevance: Rule checker in code plus state memory matches our program-decides design.

source: Besta et al. (2023) Graph of Thoughts
finding: Letting thoughts merge and refine (a graph) beats trees on tasks that split and recombine, such as sorting.
numbers: Sorting quality up 62% over ToT and 70% over CoT, cost down more than 31% versus ToT. Tasks: sorting 64 numbers, set intersection, keyword counting, document merging.
limits: Tasks chosen to be divide-and-merge friendly. Older GPT-3.5-class models.
agent_relevance: A merge operator helps only when a task splits cleanly. Not needed for open idea trees.

source: Hao et al. (2023) Reasoning with Language Model is Planning with World Model (RAP)
finding: MCTS where the LLM is both world model and reasoner beats CoT on planning, math and logic.
numbers: Blocksworld LLaMA-33B: RAP(10) 2-step 1.00, 4-step 0.86, 6-step 0.26; RAP(20) 1.00/0.88/0.42; GPT-4 CoT 0.50/0.63/0.40. Abstract: 33% relative gain over GPT-4 CoT. GSM8k: CoT 29.4, CoT+SC(10) 46.8, RAP(1) 48.6, RAP(10) 51.6. ProntoQA: CoT 87.8 answer / 64.8 proof, RAP 94.2 / 78.8.
limits: Table layout partly garbled in the text extraction; read with care. Only CoT baseline for GPT-4.
agent_relevance: The model simulates the next state and scores it; we can use real executed checks instead (G2).

source: Zhou et al. (2023) Language Agent Tree Search (LATS)
finding: MCTS with environment feedback and reflection on failed leaves beats ReAct, Reflexion, ToT and RAP in agent tasks.
numbers: HumanEval pass@1 GPT-4: base 80.1, Reflexion 91.0, LATS 92.7. GPT-3.5: CoT 46.9, ReAct 56.9, Reflexion 68.1, ToT 54.4, RAP 63.1, LATS 83.8. HotpotQA EM GPT-3.5 reasoning: CoT 0.34, ToT 0.55, RAP 0.60, LATS 0.62. Acting: ReAct 0.32, Reflexion 0.51, ToT 0.39, RAP 0.54, LATS 0.63, LATS CoT+ReAct 0.71. Game of 24 GPT-3.5: CoT 0.08, ToT 0.20, RAP 0.40, LATS 0.44.
limits: Baselines re-run by the authors. Higher compute cost; needs states that can be reverted.
agent_relevance: Real feedback from the environment is the active ingredient. Close to S6 with G2.

source: Zhou et al. (2023) LATS - sample complexity
finding: Among tree methods LATS finds answers with fewer nodes, but the gain over flat sampling at equal sample count is modest.
numbers: HotpotQA, 50 trajectories: ReAct best of 250 0.42, CoT-SC k=250 0.40, LATS n=1 0.48, ToT(ReAct) n=5 0.49, RAP 0.54, LATS n=5 0.63. LATS uses 3.55 fewer nodes than RAP and 12.12 fewer than ToT on success.
limits: Tree methods cost O(kn) samples versus O(k) for flat.
agent_relevance: Most of the gain needs a wide tree; plan for the cost.

source: Xie et al. (2023) Self-Evaluation Guided Beam Search for Reasoning
finding: Step-level self-evaluation in stochastic beam search beats Codex few-shot baselines by a few points.
numbers: Codex: GSM8K 85.5 vs 80.4, AQuA 64.2 vs 58.6, StrategyQA 77.2 vs 73.2. Llama-2 arithmetic gains at comparable budgets.
limits: Same model grades its own steps. Gains 5-10 points.
agent_relevance: Self-grading gives small gains; prefer code or tool checks (G5).

source: Sel et al. (2023) Algorithm of Thoughts
finding: Writing the search as an in-context algorithm trace matches ToT with 1 query instead of about 109.
numbers: Game of 24 GPT-4: ToT b=5 69%, 109.1 queries, 13,900 prompt and 5,500 completion tokens; AoT 71%, 1 query, 5,450 prompt and 998 completion tokens. Mini crosswords word success: ToT 46.5% with over 200 queries, AoT 52% with 2 queries, CoT-SC 15.6%. Finetune on 900 Game of 24 examples: CoT 3 to 12%, AoT 3 to 63%.
limits: ToT re-run gives 69% not 74%. One-pass search can skip branches silently.
agent_relevance: Cheap path: search inside one prompt. Test it against an explicit tree before paying for the tree.

source: Wang et al. (2024) Reasoning in Token Economies: Budget-Aware Evaluation of LLM Reasoning Strategies
finding: At matched budgets, self-consistency usually beats tree search and debate. ToT wins only with GPT-4 on Game of 24.
numbers: GPT-3.5 Game of 24: ToT lags SC by a considerable margin per query and per token. GPT-4: ToT beats the others but needs a large budget. GPT-4 ToT b=5 evaluator test, Top1: GPT-4 evaluator 0.74, random evaluator 0.0, evaluate once 0.73; GPT-3.5 for both roles 0.25.
limits: Authors used a modified evaluation prompt for GPT-3.5. Ranking depends on model and task.
agent_relevance: Compare a tree to SC at equal tokens. Evaluator quality is the key part.

source: Stechly, Valmeekam, Kambhampati (2024) On the Self-Verification Limitations of LLMs - appendix on ToT
finding: A flat set of queries with a sound external verifier almost matches ToT on Game of 24 at equal cost.
numbers: ToT costs $0.74 per problem vs $0.47 for 100 CoT prompts, about 150 CoT prompts. With 150 direct queries plus a sound verifier they reach 70% vs ToT's reported 74%.
limits: Needs a sound verifier, which Game of 24 has. Their own reading: ToT works because classical search code carries the compositional load.
agent_relevance: Backs G3/G5: the verifier and code-run search do the work.

source: Chen et al. (2024) Pairwise comparison for LLM thought evaluation (C-ToT)
finding: LLM numeric scores of thoughts are noisy. Pairwise comparison with repeated duels works better.
numbers: First task, GPT-3.5: Direct 24.8%, CoT 42.3%, SC-CoT 58.4%, S-ToT 57.1%, C-ToT standard 61.4%, C-ToT dueling 63.0%.
limits: Task names for the second table not confirmed from the extracted text. Gain over score-based ToT is about 4-6 points.
agent_relevance: If an LLM ranks ideas in S6, use repeated pairwise comparisons chosen by code, not one numeric score.

source: Snell et al. (2024) Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally
finding: With a process reward model, beam and lookahead search help at small budgets and on hard questions, but best-of-N wins at large budgets and on easy questions.
numbers: Compute-optimal allocation beats best-of-N using about 4x less compute. In a FLOPs-matched test a smaller model with test-time compute beats a 14x larger one on easy and mid questions. Beam search falls below best-of-N as budget grows. Over-optimised search gave 1-2 step short solutions.
limits: MATH, PaLM-2, trained PRM.
agent_relevance: Adapt search depth to difficulty; do not search on easy items (G1).

source: Wu et al. (2025) Inference Scaling Laws, ICLR 2025
finding: A cheap tree search (REBASE) is Pareto-optimal. MCTS costs far more and pairs badly with weighted voting.
numbers: Llemma-7B with REBASE beats Llemma-34B across all strategies on MATH500; matched accuracy with about 2x fewer FLOPs. MCTS often needs dozens of times more generated tokens than sampling.
limits: Trained reward model; math only.
agent_relevance: A small model with a good search can beat a larger one. Measure tokens per point of accuracy.

source: Katz et al. (2024) Thought of Search
finding: Ask the LLM once to write successor and goal-test code, then search in code: 100% on whole datasets with a few LLM calls.
numbers: 24 game: ToT needs about 100 LLM calls for 75% on 100 problems. Code route: 1.2 interactions for the successor function, 1 for goal test; space only 4,573 states. Mini crosswords: all 20 games solved by all 5 generated implementations, 5.5s to 346s total. They call ToT, RAP and others neither sound nor complete.
limits: Assumed 10 candidate answers per crossword clue. Needs a problem that can be coded.
agent_relevance: Strongest fit with our rule: program decides, model fills the slot (G5). Use code search where state can be coded.

source: Koh et al. (2024) Tree Search for Language Model Agents
finding: Best-first search in real web environments with an LLM value function lifts a GPT-4o agent.
numbers: VisualWebArena 26.4% success, 39.7% relative gain over no search. WebArena 19.2%, 28.0% relative gain. Gains rise with search budget.
limits: Search limited to 5 actions by compute. Absolute success is low. Needs reversible actions and a value function that is often wrong.
agent_relevance: Use real-state search for S6 only where actions can be undone.

source: Wang et al. (2024) Planning In Natural Language Improves LLM Search For Code Generation (PlanSearch)
finding: Searching over natural-language plans and observations adds diversity and lifts pass@k.
numbers: LiveCodeBench, Claude 3.5 Sonnet: PlanSearch pass@200 77.0%, repeated sampling pass@200 60.6%, no search pass@1 41.4%. Gain is predicted by an idea-diversity score.
limits: Pass@k needs tests to pick the winner.
agent_relevance: Search in idea space with measured diversity and tests; matches our idea tree.

source: Qi et al. (2024) rStar
finding: MCTS with human-like reasoning actions plus a second small model that checks trajectories lifts small models.
numbers: GSM8K: LLaMA2-7B 12.51 to 63.91, Mistral-7B 36.46 to 81.88, LLaMA3-8B-Instruct 74.53 to 91.13. Five small models, five tasks.
limits: Baseline is few-shot CoT. Agreement of two models is a hint, not proof.
agent_relevance: Second model as checker echoes G4: agreement is not independence.

source: Gandhi et al. (2024) Stream of Search
finding: Training on full search traces including backtracking beats training on the optimal path only.
numbers: Countdown: +25% search accuracy over optimal-path training; after APA and STaR finetuning it solves 36% of previously unsolved problems, including some no heuristic solver solved.
limits: Toy task, trained from scratch.
agent_relevance: Search can be written as text, but we do not train.

source: Hamm & Ajanovic (2026) Novelty-based Tree-of-Thought Search
finding: Plain ToT is fragile on Blocksworld with a small model; novelty pruning cuts cost.
numbers: Blocksworld, Qwen-14B, 50 instances: naive prompt 3/50, thinking mode 23/50. Base ToT solved 0; tuned ToT 11/50; with thinking mode 94% at 229k to 330k tokens average. Game of 24 mean effective width 1.74, 88.2% of states.
limits: Tuning on one domain. Splitting steps into separate calls made results worse.
agent_relevance: Untuned ToT can solve nothing with a small model. Low-width problems need little search.

source: Wang & Zhou (2024) Chain-of-Thought Reasoning without Prompting
finding: Branching only at the first decoding step already surfaces CoT paths.
numbers: Mistral-7B greedy 9.9%, self-consistency without CoT prompt (10 paths) 12.9%; PaLM-2 L greedy 34.8%, 40.6% with 10 paths (figures read from a garbled table).
limits: Table reading uncertain.
agent_relevance: Branching at the first choice point is cheap and supports ToT's finding that first steps decide.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
finding: Without outside feedback models cannot judge their own reasoning, so self-correction lowers accuracy. This undercuts LLM-only value functions in trees.
numbers: GPT-3.5 on GSM8K keeps its first answer 74.7% of the time; among changes, correct-to-wrong exceeds wrong-to-correct. Accuracy of all models drops across all benchmarks after intrinsic self-correction.
limits: Oracle labels would help but are not available in real use.
agent_relevance: Supports G2.

source: Besta et al. (2024) Demystifying Chains, Trees, and Graphs of Thoughts
finding: Survey with taxonomy of chain, tree and graph topologies and their cost and latency trade-offs.
numbers: Taxonomy only; no new experiments.
limits: Survey; read for vocabulary only.
agent_relevance: Use as terms for our idea tree.
